functional.text: As the user types in the search box, suggest up to 10 completions for the current prefix.
Suggestions are ranked by how popular the full query has been recently (popularity with time decay).
Trending queries (e.g. breaking news) start appearing within ~10 minutes.
Offensive or blocked queries are never suggested.

non_functional.text: Low latency: suggestions appear in < 100 ms end to end; the origin answers in < 10 ms at p99.
High availability and read-heavy: ~120k suggestion requests/s at peak; stale suggestions are acceptable, missing ones are not.
Logging searches must never slow down the search itself.

assumptions.text: 1B searches/day; about 5 suggestion requests per search after debouncing.
~100M distinct queries worth keeping after pruning rare ones; average query ~20 characters.
English only, no personalisation in v1.

out_of_scope.text: The search results page itself, spelling correction, personalised suggestions.

api.notes: Cacheable GET: CDN and browser can serve it.
Emits a query log event asynchronously; that log is the input of ranking.

data.name: prefix_index
data.why: One GET per keystroke; ~100 GB, sharded by prefix hash, rebuilt hourly into a new version.

data.name: query_log
data.fields: query, timestamp, locale (no user id needed)
data.why: Append-only input to both the batch build and the trending detector; ~100 GB/day.

data.name: query_counts
data.why: Daily aggregates so each build reads 30 small days instead of 30 days of raw logs.

data.name: trending_overlay
data.why: Small and fast-changing; merged with the main index at read time.

parts.title: Suggestion index: prefix → top 10
parts.problem: Return the 10 most popular completions for any prefix in a few milliseconds at ~120k lookups/s, from ~100M candidate queries.

options.name: SQL: WHERE query LIKE 'prefix%' ORDER BY count LIMIT 10
options.cons: scans and sorts every match: a 1-letter prefix touches millions of rows

options.name: search engine prefix / completion query
options.cons: more work per keystroke than a lookup; another cluster to run

options.name: in-memory trie with top 10 cached at every node
options.pros: one walk of len(prefix) steps, then the answer is precomputed
options.cons: custom service; memory-hungry; must be sharded and rebuilt

options.name: precomputed prefix → top 10 table in a sharded in-memory KV
options.pros: a single GET per keystroke; any KV can serve it; easy to cache at the edge
options.cons: every prefix is stored (≈100 GB); rebuilt offline

parts.choice: precomputed prefix → top 10 table (built from a trie offline) served from sharded Redis
parts.why: N1 wants a lookup, not a computation: one GET of ~1 KB. ~100 GB fits in a handful of Redis shards with replicas, and the same keys are trivially cacheable in the CDN and browser.

parts.title: Offline aggregation pipeline from query logs
parts.problem: Turn ~1B searches/day of raw query logs into ranked, filtered prefix → top 10 entries, without slowing searches and without serving a half-built index.

options.name: increment counts and update the index on every search
options.cons: a write into hot prefix rows on every search; ranking work on the search path

options.name: log searches to a stream; batch job aggregates counts with time decay and rebuilds the index
options.pros: search path only appends a log line; the index is rebuilt cleanly and swapped atomically
options.cons: the index lags by up to the build interval

parts.choice: search service appends to a Kafka query log; an hourly batch job aggregates counts with exponential decay over 30 days, filters, builds top 10 per prefix and swaps in a new index version
parts.why: Ranking by popularity only needs hour-level freshness (trending is P4). Decoupling keeps the search path a fire-and-forget append (N3), and building into a new version then flipping a pointer means readers never see a half-written index.

parts.title: Serving latency at the edge
parts.problem: Every keystroke is a request: keep suggestions under ~100 ms end to end for users worldwide and absorb peak traffic before it reaches the origin.

options.name: every keystroke goes to the origin
options.cons: ~5 requests per search; a cross-ocean round trip alone can exceed 100 ms

options.name: client debounce + browser cache
options.pros: fewer requests; repeated prefixes are free
options.cons: doesn't help the first lookup or other users

options.name: CDN caches GET /suggest?q= by prefix with a short TTL
options.pros: short prefixes (the hottest) are served from the edge near the user
options.cons: staleness up to the TTL; personalised results can't be cached

parts.choice: client debounces (~50 ms) and caches responses; CDN caches 1–3 character prefixes for 10 minutes; stateless suggest service behind a load balancer
parts.why: The shortest prefixes are both the hottest and the most shared across users, so a small edge cache removes a large share of origin traffic, and the origin only needs to serve the long tail in a few ms.

parts.title: Freshness for trending queries
parts.problem: A breaking-news query should appear in suggestions within ~10 minutes, long before the hourly rebuild includes it.

options.name: rebuild the whole index more often
options.cons: a full rebuild every few minutes is expensive and still lags

options.name: stream job counts queries in short windows and writes a small trending overlay merged at read time
options.pros: minutes of lag; tiny state; the main index is untouched
options.cons: two sources to merge; spikes need thresholds to avoid noise and abuse

parts.choice: Flink counts queries in 5-minute sliding windows, flags ones far above their baseline, and writes them to a trending overlay (prefix → hot queries, TTL 2 h); the suggest service merges overlay and index
parts.why: Only a few thousand queries trend at once, so the overlay is small and cheap to keep fresh, while the expensive index keeps its hourly cycle.

deep_dives.title: Keeping offensive queries out

options.name: filter at read time in the suggest service
options.cons: work on every request; a miss in the filter is shown to millions

options.name: filter at build time against a blocklist + classifier
options.cons: a newly-blocked query stays until the next build

options.name: both: build-time filter plus an instant read-time blocklist for emergencies
options.pros: cheap normally, instant takedown when needed

deep_dives.choice: both: build-time blocklist filter plus a small read-time emergency blocklist
deep_dives.why: F4 must hold even when the classifier misses something; the emergency list is tiny so checking it per request costs microseconds.

deep_dives.title: Swapping in a new index

options.name: update keys in place
options.cons: for minutes, readers mix old and new rankings; a failed build leaves a half-written index

options.name: write version v+1 under new keys, then flip a current-version pointer
options.pros: atomic switch; instant rollback to v

deep_dives.choice: versioned keys with an atomic pointer flip (keep v and v+1, then delete v)
deep_dives.why: N2 says stale is fine but broken is not: a flip is atomic and reversible, and the extra memory is only needed during the load.

deep_dives.title: Hot prefixes

options.name: rely on the Redis shard owning the key
options.cons: 'a', 'th' and 'how' land on single shards and dominate traffic

options.name: CDN + in-process LRU for 1–2 character prefixes
options.pros: the hottest keys never reach Redis
options.cons: minutes of staleness for those prefixes

deep_dives.choice: CDN + in-process LRU for 1–2 character prefixes
deep_dives.why: There are only a few thousand such prefixes; holding them in every suggest instance costs a few MB and removes the hot shards.

wrapup.bottlenecks: Hot short prefixes on single Redis shards (edge + in-process cache), the hourly build job (incremental daily counts), and memory for the index (prune rare queries, cap prefix length at ~20).
wrapup.failures: Redis shard down: replica promotes, CDN keeps serving short prefixes. Build fails: keep serving the current version. Kafka or Flink down: searches still work, trending pauses, the index just ages.
wrapup.monitoring: Suggest p99 latency at origin and edge, CDN hit ratio, index version age, build duration and failures, trending overlay size, suggestion click-through rate.
wrapup.scale: 10× traffic: more CDN coverage, more suggest instances and Redis replicas; 10× queries: shard the index by prefix hash and prune harder.
wrapup.future: Personalised re-ranking on top of the global list, multiple languages, typo tolerance via a search engine.
